findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is abstract and can no longer be instantiated
findings.body: `StatefulDetectorHandler` declares abstract methods (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and the newly added `build_occurrence_and_event_data`). `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` implements none of them and is just `pass`. Previously it subclassed `DetectorHandler` and only had to implement `evaluate`, which it did. Now, when `Detector.detector_handler` (src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py line 86) calls `group_type.detector_handler(self)`, instantiating this class will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class` for any Detector whose type is `metric_alert_fire`. Since `process_detectors` does not catch exceptions, this would crash the whole data-packet processing loop. If this handler is intentionally unimplemented, it should not be registered on the group type yet.

findings.title: KeyError in get_state_data when a detector defines no counter_names
findings.body: In `get_state_data`, `counter_updates` is only populated when `self.counter_names` is non-empty (line 196 `if self.counter_names:`). For any handler that returns an empty `counter_names` list (which the abstract API permits), line 222 `counter_updates[gk]` raises `KeyError` for every group key. Initialize `counter_updates` as `{gk: {} for gk in group_keys}` or use `counter_updates.get(gk, {})` so handlers with no counters work.

findings.title: Stale docstring: evaluate still documented as returning a list
findings.body: The docstring of `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` says it "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`", but the signature and implementation were changed in this PR to return a dict keyed by group key. The docstring should be updated to match, otherwise it misleads implementers of the abstract interface.

findings.title: Multi-group test builds expected occurrence with wrong value, masking value-passing bugs
findings.body: In `test_state_results_multi_group`, `group_vals` is `{"group_1": 6, "group_2": 10}`, but the expected occurrence for `group_2` is built with `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(..., "group_2", 6, ...)`. Because `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` ignores the `value` parameter entirely, this test would pass even if `evaluate_group_key_value` passed the wrong value (or a hardcoded value) to `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. There is no test anywhere that verifies the actual group value is forwarded to the occurrence hook; the helper should incorporate `value` (e.g. into the subtitle/evidence) so the contract is verified.
